answer: Here is one mechanism that works: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because mesa only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, lantern is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any cedar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
